assets: the metamodel and the rules of the standard (config/standard/)
scripts/model and its conformance measure of each system
the security system's own objects (controls, threat models, risks, vulnerabilities)
boundaries: a pull request that adds a refusal, a stage or an object and the model check that judges it
the model's measure and the people who read it as the system's posture

threats.statement: An object claims a state it has not earned, such as a threat model marked reviewed or a control marked implemented by something that does not exist. Residual: a review date and its reviewer are fields anyone can write; nothing in the tree proves the reviewer was not the author.
A change adds a refusal or a gate stage with no rule, or makes a rule name a stage the gate skips, so the standard says more than the gate enforces.
A rule or an object changes and nobody can tell which decision justified it.

A threat model or a risk records an exploitable detail of production (an endpoint's secret, a credential's location) in the public repository. Residual: the secret scans find a secret, not a described weakness; that a statement stays general, and an unfixed weakness goes to a VULN, is the reviewer's judgment.
A malformed object makes scripts/model fail, so every change that needs the model check is refused.
An element depends on a higher layer, so a lower component gains a path into one that judges it (the gate, the deploy).

findings.finding: The security test proves a review date exists, not that someone other than the author set it.
findings.reason: residual added; the review object now names the reviewer.

findings.finding: The secret scans do not judge an exploitable description.
